spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m6p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Capacity, MaxLease, MaxClock

VARIABLES reservations, free, expiry, clock

vars == <<reservations, free, expiry, clock>>

\* reservations[s] = 1 means student s currently holds a seat under a lease.
\* expiry[s] is the clock tick at which s's current lease lapses if not renewed.
\* free tracks unallocated seats directly; every action that grants or
\* reclaims a seat must move exactly one unit between "held" and "free".

Held == {s \in Students : reservations[s] = 1}

Init ==
  /\ reservations = [s \in Students |-> 0]
  /\ free = Capacity
  /\ expiry = [s \in Students |-> 0]
  /\ clock = 0

Reserve(s) ==
  /\ reservations[s] = 0
  /\ free > 0
  /\ reservations' = [reservations EXCEPT ![s] = 1]
  /\ free' = free - 1
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = clock + MaxLease]
  /\ UNCHANGED clock

Renew(s) ==
  /\ reservations[s] = 1
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = clock + MaxLease]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservations, free, clock>>

ExpireLease(s) ==
  /\ reservations[s] = 1
  /\ clock >= expiry[s]
  /\ reservations' = [reservations EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ free' = free + 1
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED clock

Release(s) ==
  /\ reservations[s] = 1
  /\ reservations' = [reservations EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ free' = free + 1
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* The admin override bypasses the expiry check but still just relocates a
\* held seat from one student to another, so it cannot inflate capacity.
AdminReassign(s1, s2) ==
  /\ s1 # s2
  /\ reservations[s1] = 1
  /\ reservations[s2] = 0
  /\ reservations' = [reservations EXCEPT ![s1] = 0, ![s2] = 1]
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![s1] = 0, ![s2] = clock + MaxLease]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<free, clock>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < MaxClock
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservations, free, expiry>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Students : Reserve(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : Renew(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : ExpireLease(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : Release(s)
  \/ \E s1 \in Students, s2 \in Students : AdminReassign(s1, s2)
  \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Core conservation claim: held seats plus free seats always equal capacity,
\* across every ordinary action and across the admin override alike.
SeatsConserved == Cardinality(Held) + free = Capacity

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Students = {s1, s2, s3}
  Capacity = 3
  MaxLease = 2
  MaxClock = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SeatsConserved
nl: A university course-registration system manages a fixed pool of seats in a single course section. A student may reserve a free seat, which grants a time-bounded lease that must later be renewed or it will lapse. A student holding a seat may renew the lease before it expires, or may voluntarily release the seat early, in both cases keeping the seat accounting consistent with the section's fixed capacity. When a global clock advances past a held seat's expiry time and the student has not renewed, the registration system automatically reclaims that seat back into the free pool. A privileged registrar may also invoke an admin override that reassigns a seat directly from one currently-enrolled student to another currently-unenrolled student, bypassing the normal expiry wait, but the override still only moves an already-allocated seat between two students rather than creating or discarding capacity. The full action set is: Reserve, Renew, ExpireLease, Release, AdminReassign, and Tick (advancing the shared clock). SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state the number of seats currently held by students plus the number of seats currently free equals the section's fixed capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m8p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Instances, Records, None, MaxVersion

ASSUME None \notin Instances

\* Two dispenser instances share one lock pool over the record set.
\* coarseLock gates which instance may even approach a slot; fineLock is the
\* inner lock that must be held across a whole read-modify-write hand-off.
\* cache remembers the version an instance last read, per record, so we can
\* tell whether a pending write would be based on a stale snapshot.

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, version, value, cache

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, version, value, cache>>

Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = [r \in Records |-> None]
    /\ fineLock = [r \in Records |-> None]
    /\ version = [r \in Records |-> 0]
    /\ value = [r \in Records |-> 0]
    /\ cache = [i \in Instances |-> [r \in Records |-> None]]

AcquireCoarse(i, r) ==
    /\ coarseLock[r] = None
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![r] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, version, value, cache>>

AcquireFine(i, r) ==
    /\ coarseLock[r] = i
    /\ fineLock[r] = None
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![r] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, version, value, cache>>

ReadRecord(i, r) ==
    /\ fineLock[r] = i
    /\ cache[i][r] = None
    /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![i][r] = version[r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, version, value>>

\* A write is only legal while the fine lock is still held, so no other
\* instance could have advanced version[r] since the cached read happened.
WriteRecord(i, r) ==
    /\ fineLock[r] = i
    /\ cache[i][r] # None
    /\ version[r] < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ value' = [value EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![i][r] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock>>

\* A pharmacist may also decide not to dispense after reading (e.g. the
\* prescription is already fulfilled); this drops the cache without a write
\* so the fine lock can still be released once version hits MaxVersion.
AbandonRead(i, r) ==
    /\ fineLock[r] = i
    /\ cache[i][r] # None
    /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![i][r] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, version, value>>

ReleaseLocks(i, r) ==
    /\ fineLock[r] = i
    /\ cache[i][r] = None
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![r] = None]
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![r] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, value, cache>>

Next ==
    \E i \in Instances, r \in Records :
        \/ AcquireCoarse(i, r)
        \/ AcquireFine(i, r)
        \/ ReadRecord(i, r)
        \/ WriteRecord(i, r)
        \/ AbandonRead(i, r)
        \/ ReleaseLocks(i, r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: any instance still nursing a cached read must still hold
\* the fine lock, and that cache must still agree with the live version -
\* i.e. nobody could have overwritten the record out from under it.
NoLostUpdate ==
    \A i \in Instances, r \in Records :
        cache[i][r] # None => (fineLock[r] = i /\ cache[i][r] = version[r])

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    i1 = i1
    i2 = i2
    r1 = r1
    r2 = r2
    NoneVal = NoneVal
    Instances = {i1, i2}
    Records = {r1, r2}
    None = NoneVal
    MaxVersion = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A pharmacy operates two independent dispenser instances that both draw from one shared pool of prescription records. Each record carries a version counter and a quantity value that dispensers must update without silently overwriting a concurrent change made by the other instance. To touch a record, a dispenser instance first acquires a coarse, pool-level lock on the record's slot, then must additionally acquire a fine-grained lock before it is allowed to read or modify the record's contents. Once holding the fine lock, an instance reads the record's current version into a private cache, then either applies its dispensing update (which advances the version and quantity together) or abandons the cached read if no dispense is needed, and finally releases the fine lock followed by the coarse lock. Because both instances draw from the very same underlying lock pool, the fine lock is the only thing standing between a stale cached read and an update that clobbers someone else's concurrent write. The full action set is: AcquireCoarse, AcquireFine, ReadRecord, WriteRecord, AbandonRead, and ReleaseLocks.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A dispenser instance holding a cached read of a prescription record can only carry that cache forward while it still holds the record's fine lock and the cached version still matches the record's live version, so neither instance ever commits a dispensing update built on a stale, overwritten read of the shared record.

spec_text:
------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m0p2t3 -------------------------
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, Hub, InitBalance, Amount, SlowBank, MaxDelay

ASSUME /\ Hub \notin Banks
       /\ SlowBank \in Banks
       /\ InitBalance \in Nat
       /\ Amount \in Nat /\ Amount <= InitBalance
       /\ MaxDelay \in Nat

Accounts == Banks \cup {Hub}

VARIABLES balance, version, phase, snap, slowDelay

vars == <<balance, version, phase, snap, slowDelay>>

\* Each account (bank or hub) has a version stamp bumped on every write.
\* A bank commits its transfer only if the versions it read still hold at
\* commit time (optimistic locking); otherwise it discards the read and retries.
\* slowDelay models a bank that is merely slow, never failed: it must still
\* eventually reach zero and commit, just after extra internal ticks.

Init ==
  /\ balance = [a \in Accounts |-> IF a = Hub THEN 0 ELSE InitBalance]
  /\ version = [a \in Accounts |-> 0]
  /\ phase = [b \in Banks |-> "idle"]
  /\ snap = [b \in Banks |-> [ownV |-> 0, hubV |-> 0]]
  /\ slowDelay = MaxDelay

ReadSnapshot(b) ==
  /\ phase[b] = "idle"
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![b] = [ownV |-> version[b], hubV |-> version[Hub]]]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "snapped"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, version, slowDelay>>

CommitTransfer(b) ==
  /\ phase[b] = "snapped"
  /\ snap[b].ownV = version[b]
  /\ snap[b].hubV = version[Hub]
  /\ (b # SlowBank \/ slowDelay = 0)
  /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![b] = @ - Amount, ![Hub] = @ + Amount]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1, ![Hub] = @ + 1]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "committed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, slowDelay>>

RetryOnConflict(b) ==
  /\ phase[b] = "snapped"
  /\ \/ snap[b].ownV # version[b]
     \/ snap[b].hubV # version[Hub]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, version, snap, slowDelay>>

DelayTick ==
  /\ phase[SlowBank] = "snapped"
  /\ slowDelay > 0
  /\ slowDelay' = slowDelay - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<balance, version, phase, snap>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Banks : ReadSnapshot(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : CommitTransfer(b)
  \/ \E b \in Banks : RetryOnConflict(b)
  \/ DelayTick

Fairness ==
  /\ \A b \in Banks : WF_vars(ReadSnapshot(b))
  /\ \A b \in Banks : WF_vars(CommitTransfer(b))
  /\ \A b \in Banks : WF_vars(RetryOnConflict(b))
  /\ WF_vars(DelayTick)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

RECURSIVE SumBal(_)
SumBal(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
             ELSE LET x == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
                  IN balance[x] + SumBal(S \ {x})

\* Conservation: nothing is created or destroyed by a commit or a retry --
\* the pool of money is just shuffled between banks and the hub.
Conservation == balance[Hub] + SumBal(Banks) = Cardinality(Banks) * InitBalance

AllSettle == \A b \in Banks : <>(phase[b] = "committed")

=======================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Banks = {b1, b2, b3}
  Hub = h
  InitBalance = 30
  Amount = 10
  SlowBank = b1
  MaxDelay = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT Conservation

PROPERTY AllSettle

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A set of banks take part in an interbank settlement batch that nets their positions into a shared clearing hub account. Every ledger row -- each bank's own account and the hub account -- carries a version counter that is bumped whenever its balance changes. To settle, a bank first takes a snapshot of its own account's version and the hub's version (ReadSnapshot), then tries to commit its transfer only if both versions still match what it read (CommitTransfer), debiting itself and crediting the hub atomically while incrementing both versions. If some other bank's settlement bumped the hub's version between the snapshot and the attempt, the compare-and-swap fails, the bank throws away its stale snapshot, and it starts over from scratch (RetryOnConflict). One designated bank is known to run slow: even once its snapshot is valid, its internal processing needs a bounded number of extra delay ticks (DelayTick) before it is allowed to commit, but it is never treated as failed and keeps making progress toward its own commit. Because commits are atomic debit-and-credit pairs against the hub, no money is ever created or destroyed by a retry, however many times it happens.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the sum of every bank's balance plus the hub's balance always equals the total of all banks' initial balances, at every reachable state including mid-retry.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bank's settlement transfer, including the slow bank's, eventually commits.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m5p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Cars, NoCar, MinCap, MaxCap

ASSUME /\ NoCar \notin Cars
       /\ MinCap \in Nat /\ MaxCap \in Nat
       /\ 1 <= MinCap /\ MinCap <= MaxCap
       /\ MaxCap = Cardinality(Cars)

VARIABLES active, capacity, candidate, votes, retired, log

vars == <<active, capacity, candidate, votes, retired, log>>

\* Quorum for the irreversible retirement scales with current bank capacity:
\* a smaller active fleet needs fewer votes to take one more car out of service.
QuorumSize(n) == (n \div 2) + 1

Init ==
  /\ active = Cars
  /\ capacity = MaxCap
  /\ candidate = NoCar
  /\ votes = {}
  /\ retired = {}
  /\ log = <<>>

ProposeRetire(c) ==
  /\ candidate = NoCar
  /\ c \in active
  /\ candidate' = c
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<active, capacity, retired, log>>

CastVote(v) ==
  /\ candidate # NoCar
  /\ v \in active
  /\ v \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {v}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<active, capacity, candidate, retired, log>>

\* The irreversible action itself: fires only once the votes collected for the
\* current candidate meet the quorum computed from the CURRENT capacity.
ExecuteRetire ==
  /\ candidate # NoCar
  /\ Cardinality(votes) >= QuorumSize(capacity)
  /\ retired' = retired \cup {candidate}
  /\ active' = active \ {candidate}
  /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
  /\ log' = Append(log, candidate)
  /\ candidate' = NoCar
  /\ votes' = {}

\* Facilities retarget the fleet's active size; only allowed between voting
\* rounds, so this is where the twist (capacity change) can move the quorum bar.
AdjustCapacity(n) ==
  /\ candidate = NoCar
  /\ n \in MinCap..MaxCap
  /\ n <= Cardinality(Cars \ retired)
  /\ active' \in {S \in SUBSET (Cars \ retired) : Cardinality(S) = n}
  /\ capacity' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<candidate, votes, retired, log>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars : ProposeRetire(c)
  \/ \E v \in Cars : CastVote(v)
  \/ ExecuteRetire
  \/ \E n \in MinCap..MaxCap : AdjustCapacity(n)

Fairness ==
  /\ WF_vars(\E v \in Cars : CastVote(v))
  /\ WF_vars(ExecuteRetire)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

\* SAFETY: the append-only retirement log never records the same car twice --
\* the irreversible action really does happen at most once per car.
NoDuplicateRetirement ==
  \A i, j \in 1..Len(log) : i # j => log[i] # log[j]

\* LIVENESS: once a car is nominated it does not stall forever mid-vote --
\* the quorum mechanism, given fair voting, always drives it to retirement.
EventualCompletion == \A c \in Cars : [](candidate = c => <>(c \in retired))

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
Cars = {c1, c2, c3}
NoCar = NoCar
MinCap = 1
MaxCap = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoDuplicateRetirement

PROPERTY EventualCompletion

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank draws from a fixed pool of cars, a subset of which are active in service at any time. Retiring a car from service permanently (structural decommissioning, not a temporary maintenance pull) requires quorum approval: any active car may be nominated as the current retirement candidate, and other active cars cast votes for that candidate. Once the number of votes reaches the quorum threshold, the retirement executes, permanently logging the car as retired and shrinking the bank's operating capacity by one. Facilities can also retarget how many cars are kept in active service, choosing any count between a configured minimum and the number of cars not yet retired, but only between voting rounds so a round's threshold never shifts underneath it. Because the quorum threshold is computed from the bank's current operating capacity rather than a fixed number, growing or shrinking the active fleet directly changes how many votes the next irreversible retirement needs. The full action set is: nominate a car as retirement candidate, cast a vote for the current candidate, execute a retirement once quorum is met, and retarget operating capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no elevator car is ever recorded as permanently retired more than once in the retirement log.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every car that becomes a retirement candidate is eventually actually retired.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m9p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT MaxEpoch

VARIABLES ctrlEpoch, robotEpoch, inbox, dropCount, issued

vars == <<ctrlEpoch, robotEpoch, inbox, dropCount, issued>>

Epochs == 0..MaxEpoch
Kinds == {"Reconf", "Drop"}
Messages == [epoch: Epochs, kind: Kinds]

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the controller bumps ctrlEpoch and
\* broadcasts a Reconf message; the robot only adopts a Reconf that
\* strictly advances its own fence, so a reordered or duplicated
\* announcement can never push the fence backward.

TypeOK ==
  /\ ctrlEpoch \in Epochs
  /\ robotEpoch \in Epochs
  /\ inbox \subseteq Messages
  /\ dropCount \in 0..2
  /\ issued \subseteq Epochs

Init ==
  /\ ctrlEpoch = 0
  /\ robotEpoch = 0
  /\ inbox = {}
  /\ dropCount = 0
  /\ issued = {}

Reconfigure ==
  /\ ctrlEpoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ ctrlEpoch' = ctrlEpoch + 1
  /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[epoch |-> ctrlEpoch + 1, kind |-> "Reconf"]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<robotEpoch, dropCount, issued>>

IssueDropCmd ==
  /\ dropCount = 0
  /\ ctrlEpoch \notin issued
  /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[epoch |-> ctrlEpoch, kind |-> "Drop"]}
  /\ issued' = issued \cup {ctrlEpoch}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ctrlEpoch, robotEpoch, dropCount>>

\* Messages are never removed from inbox on delivery, so any message can
\* be redelivered later -- this models reordering, delay and duplication
\* all at once: delivery order is fully nondeterministic.
DeliverReconf ==
  \E m \in inbox :
    /\ m.kind = "Reconf"
    /\ m.epoch > robotEpoch
    /\ robotEpoch' = m.epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ctrlEpoch, inbox, dropCount, issued>>

\* The epoch fence: a Drop is honored only when its tag matches the
\* robot's current fence AND the pallet has not already been dropped.
\* A stale (old-epoch) or duplicate Drop message is simply never
\* matched and so can never re-trigger the irreversible action.
DeliverDrop ==
  \E m \in inbox :
    /\ m.kind = "Drop"
    /\ m.epoch = robotEpoch
    /\ dropCount = 0
    /\ dropCount' = dropCount + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ctrlEpoch, robotEpoch, inbox, issued>>

Next == Reconfigure \/ IssueDropCmd \/ DeliverReconf \/ DeliverDrop

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: the irreversible pallet-drop fires at most once, even though
\* Reconf/Drop messages can be delivered out of order, late, or twice.
DropAtMostOnce == dropCount <= 1

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  MaxEpoch = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT DropAtMostOnce

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A fleet controller manages a single warehouse robot tasked with dropping a pallet into a delivery bay, an action that cannot be undone once performed. The controller periodically reconfigures the system by advancing a monotonically increasing epoch number and broadcasting the new epoch to the robot as a Reconf message. Once it decides the drop is warranted for the current epoch, the controller sends a Drop command tagged with that same epoch number. The underlying network can reorder, delay, or duplicate any in-flight message, so the robot may receive its Reconf and Drop messages in any order and may see the same message more than once. The robot only advances its local epoch fence when it receives a Reconf message whose epoch is strictly greater than its current fence, so the fence can never move backward even under reordering. The robot performs the pallet drop only when a delivered Drop message's epoch exactly matches its current fence and the drop has not already occurred. The full action set is: the controller advancing its epoch and announcing it (Reconfigure), the controller issuing a fenced Drop command for the current epoch (IssueDropCmd), the robot adopting a newer epoch from a delivered Reconf message (DeliverReconf), and the robot executing the drop upon a matching, non-stale Drop message (DeliverDrop).
SAFETY PROPERTY: The pallet drop action executes at most once, no matter how controller-to-robot messages are reordered, delayed, or duplicated.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m2p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, NumBlocks, Cap

ASSUME NumBlocks \in Nat \ {0}
ASSUME Cap \in Nat \ {0}
ASSUME Cardinality(Trains) <= NumBlocks

Blocks == 1 .. NumBlocks
Succ(b) == IF b = NumBlocks THEN 1 ELSE b + 1

VARIABLES pos, tstate, vote, dest

vars == <<pos, tstate, vote, dest>>

\* Two-phase commit per train: the current block is the coordinator, the
\* destination block's controller is the sole participant. A "yes" vote
\* reserves a capacity slot immediately; commit only converts that
\* reservation into physical occupancy, it never adds a fresh unit of load.

InitBlock == CHOOSE b \in Blocks : TRUE

\* Trains start one-per-block (an injection exists since Trains fits in
\* Blocks) so the very first state already respects capacity.
InitPos == CHOOSE f \in [Trains -> Blocks] :
              \A x, y \in Trains : x # y => f[x] # f[y]

Occupied(b) == Cardinality({t \in Trains : pos[t] = b})
Reserved(b) == Cardinality({t \in Trains :
                  /\ dest[t] = b /\ tstate[t] = "prepare" /\ vote[t] = "yes"})
Load(b) == Occupied(b) + Reserved(b)

Init ==
  /\ pos = InitPos
  /\ tstate = [t \in Trains |-> "idle"]
  /\ vote = [t \in Trains |-> "none"]
  /\ dest = InitPos

RequestMove(t) ==
  /\ tstate[t] = "idle"
  /\ dest' = [dest EXCEPT ![t] = Succ(pos[t])]
  /\ tstate' = [tstate EXCEPT ![t] = "prepare"]
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![t] = "pending"]
  /\ UNCHANGED pos

\* The participant may cast this vote arbitrarily many steps after the
\* prepare request -- it is slow, not failed -- but while pending, no
\* other action lets the requesting train advance.
Vote(t) ==
  /\ tstate[t] = "prepare"
  /\ vote[t] = "pending"
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![t] = IF Load(dest[t]) < Cap THEN "yes" ELSE "no"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, tstate, dest>>

Commit(t) ==
  /\ tstate[t] = "prepare"
  /\ vote[t] = "yes"
  /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = dest[t]]
  /\ tstate' = [tstate EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
  /\ dest' = [dest EXCEPT ![t] = InitBlock]

Abort(t) ==
  /\ tstate[t] = "prepare"
  /\ vote[t] = "no"
  /\ tstate' = [tstate EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![t] = "none"]
  /\ dest' = [dest EXCEPT ![t] = InitBlock]
  /\ UNCHANGED pos

Next == \E t \in Trains : RequestMove(t) \/ Vote(t) \/ Commit(t) \/ Abort(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: physical occupancy of every block stays within its declared
\* capacity, even though a slow participant may leave votes pending
\* indefinitely -- slowness blocks progress, it never bypasses the vote.
CapacityOK == \A b \in Blocks : Occupied(b) <= Cap

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityOK

CONSTANTS
  t1 = t1
  t2 = t2
  t3 = t3
  Trains = {t1, t2, t3}
  NumBlocks = 3
  Cap = 2
nl:
A subway line is divided into a small ring of signalling blocks, each guarded by its own local signalling controller and physically able to hold only a limited number of trains at once. When a train wants to advance from its current block into the next block on the ring, its controller acts as a two-phase-commit coordinator: it sends a prepare request to the destination block's controller, which is the sole participant deciding whether room exists. The participant computes the block's current load -- trains physically present plus trains already reserved via an earlier yes vote -- and answers yes only if that load is still below the block's capacity, otherwise it answers no. The coordinator may only advance the train into the block once the participant's yes vote has been received; a no vote causes the coordinator to abandon the attempt and return the train to idle so it can retry later. Crucially, the destination participant is never assumed to fail: it may simply be slow, leaving its vote pending for an arbitrary number of steps while other trains continue to request moves, vote, commit, or abort elsewhere, but a pending vote can never be treated as an implicit yes and never lets the requesting train slip into the block unauthorized. Because a yes vote reserves capacity the instant it is cast, and a commit only converts that existing reservation into physical occupancy rather than adding a fresh unit of load, no sequence of interleaved requests, slow votes, commits, and aborts can ever push a block's train count past its declared capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No signalling block ever holds more trains than its declared physical capacity, regardless of how long any participant's vote remains pending.
